title: Can Babies Have Mental Health? Infant Mental Health and Attachment Explained

sentences.en: Can a baby have mental health before they can even talk?
sentences.zh: 婴儿在甚至还不会说话之前，就会有心理健康问题吗？

sentences.en: It sounds like a strange question, but babies are constantly communicating, learning, and building relationships long before they have the words to tell us how they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一个奇怪的问题，但在婴儿拥有表达内心感受的词汇之前，他们其实一直在不断地交流、学习和建立关系。

sentences.en: And those earliest interactions may matter far more than most of us realize.
sentences.zh: 而那些最早期的互动可能比我们大多数人意识到的要重要得多。

sentences.en: So today I'm joined by fellow clinical psychologist, Dr. Charlotte Dunster-Page.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我邀请到了同行兼临床心理学家夏洛特·邓斯特-佩吉博士。

sentences.en: As we look at infant mental health, attachment, bonding, and what happens when things don't quite go to plan.
sentences.zh: 我们将共同探讨婴儿心理健康、依恋、情感纽带，以及当事情没有按计划进行时会发生什么。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent and this is Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，欢迎收听《心理学其实》。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《心理学其实》。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Very excited to have along here our guest today, a fellow clinical psychologist, Dr. Charlotte Dunster-Page.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴今天能请到我们的嘉宾，同行兼临床心理学家夏洛特·邓斯特-佩吉博士。

sentences.en: Hi, Charlotte.
sentences.zh: 嗨，夏洛特。

sentences.en: Hello, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 你好，谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你抽空参加。

sentences.en: And we are talking today about all things infant mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们今天讨论的话题全都是关于婴儿心理健康的。

sentences.en: So let's dive right in.
sentences.zh: 那我们就直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: Let's go first off with a quick fire round.
sentences.zh: 首先我们来玩个快问快答环节。

sentences.en: Okay, question one.
sentences.zh: 好的，第一个问题。

sentences.en: Can an infant have their own mental health?
sentences.zh: 婴儿会有他们自己的心理健康状态吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: And I could talk probably for an hour or two about this alone.
sentences.zh: 光是这一点，我大概就能独自讲上一两个小时。

sentences.en: But I think one of the things that's really helpful to think about is when we colloquially, in general everyday conversations, when we think about mental health,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，有一个非常有帮助的思考角度是：在我们的日常俗语和普通对话中谈到心理健康时，

sentences.en: we're not, as a society, very good at separating out mental health versus mental health problems versus diagnosable mental health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 作为整个社会，我们并不太擅长区分“心理健康”、“心理健康问题”与“可诊断的心理健康问题”。

sentences.en: And yet, if we think about things from a physical health kind of comparison, that is often helpful.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们用身体健康来进行类比，通常就会很有帮助。

sentences.en: So any of us on any given day have a state of physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们任何人在任何特定的日子里都有一种身体健康的状况。

sentences.en: You know, we might have a cold or just feel a bit under the weather or be really tired that day.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们可能感冒了，或者只是觉得有点不舒服，又或者那天真的很累。

sentences.en: So most of us on any given day would be able to say that we feel zero out of 10, 10 out of 10 in terms of our physical health.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们大多数人在任何特定日子里都可以用从0到10的分数来评估自己的身体健康状况。

sentences.en: But it has to cross a certain threshold before we talk about having a physical health problem.
sentences.zh: 但它必须跨越某个特定的门槛，我们才会称之为遇到了身体健康问题。

sentences.en: And then we might be under hospital or GP or something before we have a diagnosable physical health problem.
sentences.zh: 然后，在我们遇到可诊断的身体健康问题之前，我们可能会去医院、看全科医生或者接受某种治疗。

sentences.en: So we've got that kind of scale.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这样一种衡量标准。

sentences.en: And mental health is the same.
sentences.zh: 心理健康也是如此。

sentences.en: And so everybody, whether they're a baby or of any age, we all have a state of well-being on any given day, a state of mental well-being.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个人，无论是婴儿还是任何年龄段的人，在任何特定的日子里，我们都有一种健康状态，一种心理健康状态。

sentences.en: And so a baby has a state of mental well-being on any given day that fluctuates moment to moment, day by day.
sentences.zh: 所以，婴儿在任何特定的日子里也有一种心理健康状态，它会随着时间和日常而不断波动。

sentences.en: And then babies can have mental health problems as well.
sentences.zh: 而且婴儿同样也会有心理健康问题。

sentences.en: What we don't usually talk about is babies having diagnosable mental health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们通常不怎么讨论的是婴儿患有可诊断的心理健康问题。

sentences.en: But there can be issues with a baby's mental well-being.
sentences.zh: 但婴儿的心理健康确实可能会出现状况。

sentences.en: And so that absolutely can happen for babies.
sentences.zh: 所以这在婴儿身上是完全可能发生的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'm sure we'll go much deeper on lots of those areas.
sentences.zh: 我确信我们接下来会深入探讨其中的许多方面。

sentences.en: Let's go on with quickfire around question two.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续快问快答的第二个问题。

sentences.en: Is it possible that as a parent, someone's had really quite a tricky time of it, kind of mental health and developmental wise themselves.
sentences.zh: 作为父母，某人在心理健康和成长发展方面可能经历过非常棘手的一段时期，这是否可能发生？

sentences.en: But is it possible that their child could have a very different experience and maybe not have the mental health wobbles that they've had?
sentences.zh: 但他们的孩子是否可能拥有截然不同的体验，也许并不会经历他们曾经经历过的心理健康波动？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全有可能。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't work in my field if that wasn't possible.
sentences.zh: 如果这是不可能的，我就不会从事我这个领域的工作了。

sentences.en: Like the work that I do, working with parents and infants in their earliest years, offering that parent infant therapy, that support.
sentences.zh: 就像我所做的工作，在最早的几年里为父母和婴儿提供支持，提供父母-婴儿疗法以及相关支持。

sentences.en: If there was no possibility of that baby having a different experience to the parent, then there wouldn't be a need for my job.
sentences.zh: 如果这个婴儿完全没有可能拥有与父母不同的体验，那么我的工作就没有存在的必要了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，完全有可能。

sentences.en: That is the absolute aim of the work that I do is working with parents and babies to help that baby develop in the way that that parent absolutely wants them to,
sentences.zh: 我所做的工作的绝对目标就是与父母和婴儿合作，帮助婴儿按照父母内心深处期望的那样去成长，

sentences.en: even though that parent might have had some difficult experiences themselves.
sentences.zh: 尽管这位父母自己可能经历过一些困难。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I know a really common question, certainly from people perhaps earlier in their career, is do you have to be a parent to work as an effective clinician in this area?
sentences.zh: 我知道一个非常常见的问题，尤其是来自那些职业生涯较早阶段的人，那就是：要想成为这个领域里称职的临床医生，你必须得先成为父母吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's really interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，这真的很有意思，不是吗？

sentences.en: I absolutely started in this field before becoming a parent.
sentences.zh: 我成为父母之前就绝对已经开始在这个领域工作了。

sentences.en: So, no, I don't think that you have to be.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，我认为并非必须如此。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people would say it makes quite a bit of a difference and it helps.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人会说这确实有不小的区别而且会有所帮助。

sentences.en: I personally think that you're bringing different skills and that maybe having some of that insight can be helpful, but you can get that from elsewhere as well.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为你带来的是不同的技能，而且拥有某些这样的洞察力可能会有帮助，但你也可以从其他地方获得这些。

sentences.en: You can have siblings and cousins and work with babies in other ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以有兄弟姐妹和表亲，也可以通过其他方式与婴儿共事。

sentences.en: It's certainly being a parent gives you a certain insight into what other parents are dealing with and coping with.
sentences.zh: 成为父母确实能让你对其他父母正在应对和处理的事情有某种独特的洞察。

sentences.en: But I don't think it's a prerequisite at all.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这绝对不是一个先决条件。

sentences.en: And absolutely, I was working with families before becoming a mum myself.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，在我自己成为母亲之前，我就已经在和各个家庭合作了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I was as well.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: My first job was qualified in CAMHS for almost four years.
sentences.zh: 我合格后的第一份工作是在儿童和青少年心理健康服务机构（CAMHS）工作了近四年。

sentences.en: Question four, is infant mental health something that you wish was more at the forefront of people supporting those who are care experienced?
sentences.zh: 第四个问题，你是否希望婴儿心理健康问题能更多地成为那些为有看护经历者提供支持的人员的首要关注点？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对的。

sentences.en: It's something that I wish was more at the forefront of everything, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我希望它能成为所有工作首要关注的焦点。

sentences.en: Even within clinical psychology, doctoral training, it's not part of our core training in most of the courses nationally.
sentences.zh: 即使在临床心理学和博士培训中，它也不是全国大多数课程的核心培训内容。

sentences.en: It is, we're talking in my field about something called the baby blind spot.
sentences.zh: 在我们这个领域，我们正在讨论一个叫做“婴儿盲点”的概念。

sentences.en: So this is the idea that everything from policy in government to services within the NHS usually don't consider the needs of babies when writing those policies,
sentences.zh: 这就是这样一种观点：从政府的政策到国民医疗服务体系（NHS）内部的服务，在撰写这些政策时通常都不会考虑婴儿的需求，

sentences.en: when developing those services.
sentences.zh: 在开发这些服务时也是如此。

sentences.en: It's rare that babies are considered.
sentences.zh: 很少有人会考虑到婴儿。

sentences.en: We might think about older people, working age adults.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会想到老年人、适龄工作成人。

sentences.en: We might think about children and teenagers, but rarely do we think about babies.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会想到儿童和青少年，但我们很少会想到婴儿。

sentences.en: And in terms of thinking about care leave specifically, I think our attachment experiences are influenced by our parenting or our cared for experiences.
sentences.zh: 具体谈到看护假时，我认为我们的依恋体验会受到我们的育儿经历或被看护经历的影响。

sentences.en: So if we have that experience of being in care, then it's likely that that is going to have that impact on our well-being as an adult.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们有过被看护的经历，那么这很可能会对我们成年后的幸福感产生影响。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，绝对如此。

sentences.en: I think anybody who works with babies or anybody who works with people who have experienced adversity in their early years, which is likely to include a lot of care leavers,
sentences.zh: 我认为任何与婴儿共事的人，或者任何与那些在早年经历过逆境的人共事的人——这很可能包括许多曾经受过看护的离开者——

sentences.en: I wish all of those professionals were able to learn more about infant mental health.
sentences.zh: 我希望所有这些专业人士都能够多了解一些关于婴儿心理健康的知识。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Just thinking about my own experiences of having had two children.
sentences.zh: 回想我自己抚养两个孩子的经历。

sentences.en: I'm aware that the National Childbirth Trust, often called the NCT, have a focus on the first 1,001 days.
sentences.zh: 我知道英国国家生育信托基金（通常被称为NCT）非常关注最初的1001天。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a bit more about why that is and why it matters?
sentences.zh: 你能为我们多讲讲为什么会这样以及它为什么重要吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没问题，当然可以。

sentences.en: So 1,001 days is roughly, everybody's experience is obviously different, but it's roughly the number of days from conception until a baby's second birthday.
sentences.zh: 所以1001天大约是——每个人的经历显然都不同——但它大致是从受孕到婴儿两岁生日之间的天数。

sentences.en: And what we know about why this is so important is that essentially the time that we don't remember as humans is the most influential time in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的为什么这如此重要的原因是，本质上作为人类，我们不记得的那段时期是我们一生中最具影响力的时期。

sentences.en: How people relate to us, how people care for us, how people treat us during that first 1,001 days influences who we are throughout the rest of our lives,
sentences.zh: 在这最初的1001天里，人们如何与我们互动、如何照顾我们、如何对待我们，会影响我们一生中成为什么样的人，

sentences.en: including how we'll relate to others, what kind of job we get, our position in society.
sentences.zh: 包括我们将如何与他人建立关系、我们从事什么样的工作、我们在社会中的地位。

sentences.en: Things like earnings and things like earnings and things like that, our learning, our education.
sentences.zh: 诸如收入之类的事情以及诸如此类的收入问题，我们的学习，我们的教育。

sentences.en: A lot of these things are influenced before we even turned two years old.
sentences.zh: 许多这样的事情在我们甚至还没满两岁之前就已经受到影响了。

sentences.en: So, yes, the first 1,001 days, it's a period of neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，最初的1001天是一个神经可塑性时期。

sentences.en: So our brains are most malleable during this period.
sentences.zh: 因此，在此期间我们的大脑可塑性最强。

sentences.en: We can learn really, really well and really quickly and really extensively during this period.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，我们可以非常、非常出色、非常迅速且非常广泛地进行学习。

sentences.en: And the reason that myself and others like me work in this field is that not only is the baby most able to change and adapt during this period,
sentences.zh: 我和其他像我一样的人之所以在这个领域工作，是因为在此期间不仅婴儿最具改变和适应能力，

sentences.en: but often parents are as well because there is nothing more motivating than being about to welcome a baby into the world to wanting to make changes in your own life.
sentences.zh: 而且往往父母也是如此，因为没有什么比即将迎来一个新生命更能激发人们想要改变自己生活的动力了。

sentences.en: So it is often this wonderfully wonderful period where both parents and child are able to change things and make a difference to their lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，这通常是一个美妙绝伦的时期，在这个时期，父母和孩子都能够改变现状，为他们的生活带来改变。

sentences.en: And it's wonderful to work with and see.
sentences.zh: 参与其中并亲眼见证这一切真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: So nice.
sentences.zh: 太美好了。

sentences.en: And what a lovely springboard into the main topic of our episode as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们这期节目主题的一个绝佳切入点。

sentences.en: So thank you, Charlotte.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你，夏洛特。

sentences.en: Let's imagine then that someone watching or listening to this is a parent and they're starting to wonder whether maybe all is not well with their own attachment with the baby
sentences.zh: 那么让我们想象一下，收看或收听节目的某位观众或听众是一位父母，他们开始怀疑自己与婴儿的情感纽带是否出了问题，

sentences.en: or the baby's just not feeling like they're thriving.
sentences.zh: 或者觉得婴儿的状态似乎并没有蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: What kind of signs and symptoms might they be picking up on?
sentences.zh: 他们可能会注意到哪些迹象和症状呢？

sentences.en: So we have kind of an idea of what that might look like in a parent and a baby.
sentences.zh: 所以我们大致了解这在父母和婴儿身上可能会是什么样的表现。

sentences.en: And we might ask the parents some questions.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会向父母问一些问题。

sentences.en: We might observe the baby.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会观察婴儿。

sentences.en: One of the things that in my field we often find is that parents who are really struggling might not be in a position to recognise the struggles.
sentences.zh: 在我的领域中，我们经常发现的一个现象是，那些真正挣扎的父母可能无法意识到这些挣扎。

sentences.en: And often the parents who wonder if they're doing a good job might be the ones that actually are.
sentences.zh: 而往往那些担心自己是否做得好的父母，反而是真正做得不错的那些人。

sentences.en: I think there's an old saying of the fact that you're worrying about being a good mum probably means you are.
sentences.zh: 我想有一句老话说过，你担心自己是不是个好妈妈，这大概就意味着你确实是个好妈妈。

sentences.en: And that's not to dismiss the challenges of the families that I work with where they really are struggling.
sentences.zh: 这并不是要忽视我所服务的那些真正陷入挣扎的家庭所面临的挑战。

sentences.en: Everybody is bringing their own stuff, their own difficulties to the journey.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在将他们自己的问题、他们自己的困难带入这段旅程中。

sentences.en: But what I would say is that we all have difficulties in relationships at times, whether that's our romantic partner, our colleagues, our friends, our children as well.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，我们在人际关系中有时都会遇到困难，无论是与我们的浪漫伴侣、我们的同事、我们的朋友，还是我们的孩子。

sentences.en: No relationship is completely smooth.
sentences.zh: 没有任何一段关系是完全一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: And if we're experiencing some challenges on a day to day basis with our newborn baby, with our toddler, that's probably really, really normal.
sentences.zh: 如果我们与新生儿、与幼儿在日常生活中经历一些挑战，那可能真的、真的很正常。

sentences.en: You know, being a parent is incredibly challenging.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为人父母具有难以置信的挑战性。

sentences.en: So there's an element of that, I suppose, first of all, to kind of reassure.
sentences.zh: 我想，首先这也是为了起到一点安慰作用。

sentences.en: But if a parent is really worried about their bond with their baby or the baby's attachment with them, then absolutely seeking support is really, really important.
sentences.zh: 但如果父母真的对他们与宝宝之间的纽带或宝宝对他们的依恋感到担忧，那么寻求支持就真的、真的很重要。

sentences.en: And the earlier that's possible, then the better.
sentences.zh: 而且越早越好。

sentences.en: And that might be the parent recognising that they aren't feeling as positively towards the baby as they hoped to.
sentences.zh: 这可能表现为父母意识到自己对婴儿并没有产生如预期那般积极的感受。

sentences.en: We see on the media, don't we, this kind of shiny birth with white sheets and nobody's screaming too much and everything's wonderful and clean and shiny.
sentences.zh: 我们在媒体上经常看到那种铺着白床单、光鲜亮丽的分娩场景，没有人叫喊得太厉害，一切都那么美好、干净和光鲜。

sentences.en: And then the baby's placed in their arms and parents falling in love with baby instantly.
sentences.zh: 然后婴儿被放在他们怀里，父母瞬间就爱上了婴儿。

sentences.en: And that can happen for some people.
sentences.zh: 这对于某些人来说确实会发生。

sentences.en: But the reality is that relationship is like any relationship.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，这种关系就像任何关系一样。

sentences.en: It takes some time to build and you don't have to fall in love with your baby the moment that they're placed in your arms to develop that positive bond with baby at the time.
sentences.zh: 它需要时间来建立，你并不非得在宝宝被放到你怀里的那一刻就爱上他们，才能在当时与宝宝建立起积极的纽带。

sentences.en: What we want to see, what we hope that all babies experience is attuned, sensitive care.
sentences.zh: 我们希望看到的是，我们希望所有婴儿都能体验到的是和谐、敏感的照料。

sentences.en: So if a parent is able to be, to kind of read the signs of what their baby's telling them and be sensitive to them,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果父母能够去解读宝宝向他们传达的信号，并对这些信号保持敏感，

sentences.en: then the chances are that attachment is going to grow in that positive way.
sentences.zh: 那么这种依恋朝积极方向发展的几率就会很高。

sentences.en: But it's also really important to say on that, that that is not 100% of the time.
sentences.zh: 但同样非常重要的一点是要说明，这种情况并不是100%的。

sentences.en: There will absolutely be times where a parent is trying to figure out what is going on for their baby and can't.
sentences.zh: 绝对会有那么一些时刻，父母试图弄清楚他们的宝宝到底怎么了，却无能为力。

sentences.en: We just don't always know what is going on for our babies every step of the way.
sentences.zh: 我们并不总能每时每刻都知道宝宝究竟在经历什么。

sentences.en: If you're struggling to understand what your baby is needing, that's not a problem.
sentences.zh: 如果你很难理解你的宝宝需要什么，这不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: It's probably normal.
sentences.zh: 这可能很正常。

sentences.en: And equally, if we, as parents, if we, for whatever reason, cannot respond sensitively to our baby's needs all of the time, again, probably normal.
sentences.zh: 同样地，如果我们作为父母，无论出于何种原因，无法做到时时刻刻对宝宝的需求做出敏感的反应，这再次说明，大概也很正常。

sentences.en: But sometimes there are things in our own lives, whether that's our mental health, our own experiences of how we were parented when we were small, social factors, these things,
sentences.zh: 但有时我们生活中的某些事情，无论是我们的心理健康、我们自己小时候被抚养方式的经历，还是社会因素，这些事情，

sentences.en: if they're getting in the way of how we respond and attune to our babies, then that might be the time to kind of, to see support.
sentences.zh: 如果它们妨碍了我们对宝宝做出反应和产生共鸣，那么这可能就是寻求支持的时候了。

sentences.en: Yeah, really, really important.
sentences.zh: 是的，真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And I think often, I think back to when I first found out I was pregnant with my eldest child, actually even before, because he was a, he was a tried for baby.
sentences.zh: 我想经常，我会回想起我第一次得知自己怀上大宝的时候，其实甚至在怀孕之前，因为他是一个我们渴望要的孩子。

sentences.en: I definitely had to learn how to become a mother, which meant reading pregnancy magazines, which meant taking all my, you know, nutrition just, just so,
sentences.zh: 我绝对必须学习如何成为一名母亲，这意味着阅读怀孕杂志，这意味着确保我的营养摄入万无一失，

sentences.en: and very much thinking about what kind of parent I wanted to be with a very intentional way.
sentences.zh: 并且非常刻意地思考我想成为什么样类型的父母。

sentences.en: And when I was pregnant with the second one, I noticed I didn't really do that.
sentences.zh: 而且当我怀第二个孩子时，我发现自己其实并没有那样做。

sentences.en: And I think I gave myself a bit of a hard time about that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我当时对自己有点过于严厉了。

sentences.en: But at no point did I say, well, of course you don't really need to do that because you already know how to be a mother.
sentences.zh: 但我在任何时候都没有说过，嗯，你当然不需要那样做，因为你已经知道怎么当妈妈了。

sentences.en: You've already really enjoyed mothering your eldeSt.
sentences.zh: 你其实已经非常享受带大宝的过程了。

sentences.en: So maybe just really enjoy where you are right now.
sentences.zh: 所以也许只要好好享受你现在的状态就好了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It's such a different journey for first baby versus subsequent babies.
sentences.zh: 照顾第一个孩子和照顾后面的孩子，这段旅程有着天壤之别。

sentences.en: And a different process that people go through.
sentences.zh: 这也是人们需要经历的不同过程。

sentences.en: There's also differences with, say, it's mum and dad.
sentences.zh: 比方说，爸爸和妈妈之间也会存在差异。

sentences.en: If mum's pregnant and dad is not pregnant.
sentences.zh: 如果妈妈怀孕了而爸爸没有怀孕。

sentences.en: And the differences in bonding potentially for mum and dad, that can be there as well.
sentences.zh: 而且妈妈和爸爸在建立亲子关系方面潜在的差异，也是可能存在的。

sentences.en: You know, as a, as a birthing mum, we have that opportunity to carry our babies for nine months.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为经历分娩的妈妈，我们有机会怀胎九个月。

sentences.en: They're with us.
sentences.zh: 他们一直和我们在一起。

sentences.en: They are there during our carrying on through work periods and having a bad day and chatting to the baby and on a drive and telling the baby about your day and all those things that we can do just to start and build that relationship with our baby.
sentences.zh: 在我们继续上班、经历糟糕的一天、和宝宝聊天、在开车时告诉宝宝你这一天过得怎么样，以及所有那些我们能做的事情中，他们都在那里，以此来开始并建立我们与宝宝之间的关系。

sentences.en: And dads don't get that.
sentences.zh: 而爸爸们则没有这种体验。

sentences.en: So sometimes it can take longer for dads to bond after a baby's born.
sentences.zh: 所以有时在宝宝出生后，爸爸们可能需要更长的时间来建立亲子关系。

sentences.en: And that's really normal.
sentences.zh: 这真的很正常。

sentences.en: And equally with second babies and subsequent babies after a second, life can be pretty busy if you've already got that first baby.
sentences.zh: 同样地，对于第二个孩子以及老二之后的其他孩子，如果你已经有了大宝，生活可能会相当忙碌。

sentences.en: So you might not spend that intentional time of going to antenatal classes, NCT classes, chatting to your baby that's in the womb still,
sentences.zh: 所以你可能不会特意花时间去上产前班、NCT课程，或者跟还在子宫里的宝宝聊天，

sentences.en: because you've probably got your eldest in the car and you're chatting to them instead.
sentences.zh: 因为你可能正把老大放在车里，转而跟他们聊天。

sentences.en: So there can be sometimes less of that intentional time spent together with your unborn baby.
sentences.zh: 因此，与未出生的宝宝一起度过的这种刻意时间有时可能会减少。

sentences.en: So it can be a bit more of a, oh, gosh, they're here.
sentences.zh: 所以可能会有一种“天哪，他们出生了”的感觉。

sentences.en: And now I've got to get to know this baby.
sentences.zh: 现在我得开始了解这个宝宝了。

sentences.en: But so it absolutely does not need to be this perfect, magical falling in love moment, the moment they're born.
sentences.zh: 但是，这绝对不需要是一见钟情那种完美、神奇的时刻，就在他们出生的一瞬间。

sentences.en: It's a relationship.
sentences.zh: 这是一种关系。

sentences.en: It takes time that you build it slowly with your baby over those first weeks and months of life.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间，需要在宝宝生命最初的几周和几个月里，慢慢与宝宝建立起来。

sentences.en: Yeah, I might give you a little real life case study.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来分享一个小型的真实生活案例。

sentences.en: I've never spoken about this anywhere publicly before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未在任何公开场合谈论过这件事。

sentences.en: So this is our first time.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们的第一次。

sentences.en: But I've got two boys and we didn't find out either time.
sentences.zh: 但我有两个男孩，而且我们两次都没有提前知道性别。

sentences.en: I ended up with emergency sections for both of them.
sentences.zh: 我生两个孩子时最后都做了紧急剖腹产。

sentences.en: So when my youngest was placed on me and we were told he was a little boy, like, honestly, I don't think I've ever been happier in my life.
sentences.zh: 所以当我的小儿子被放在我身上，我们被告知他是个小男孩时，说实话，我觉得我一生中从未这么开心过。

sentences.en: Me and my husband were both completely thrilled because we wanted two boys.
sentences.zh: 我和丈夫都兴奋极了，因为我们想要两个男孩。

sentences.en: And I stayed on that really high cloud until the next day, I would say, when just before our appointment to be dispatched out of the hospital,
sentences.zh: 我那种极度快乐的状态一直持续到第二天，可以说，就在我们准备办理出院手续的预约之前，

sentences.en: we had a junior doctor come in and do our kind of checks before we left.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位初级医生进来，在我们离开前做了一下常规检查。

sentences.en: And it turns out that what we thought was normal post-delivery swelling in my son was an inguinal hernia.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，我们原以为是我儿子分娩后正常的产后肿胀，其实是一个腹股沟疝。

sentences.en: And the junior doctor hadn't experienced that before, so didn't know quite what to do.
sentences.zh: 这位初级医生以前没遇到过这种情况，所以不太知道该怎么处理。

sentences.en: And so had said, you might have to go in a blue light to Birmingham Children's right now.
sentences.zh: 于是他说，你现在可能得坐救护车紧急去伯明翰儿童医院了。

sentences.en: So call your husband.
sentences.zh: 所以快给你丈夫打电话。

sentences.en: So obviously that's quite different than cloud nine to there.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这和极度快乐的心情有很大落差。

sentences.en: That was like a lot of adjustment.
sentences.zh: 那需要进行大量的心理调整。

sentences.en: And then, oh, it's a bit emotional, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 然后，哦，这挺让人情绪激动的，不是吗？

sentences.en: But I was really quite upset for quite a few days.
sentences.zh: 但我在好几天里确实都非常难过。

sentences.en: We didn't go home for a bit because I felt like I needed to learn how to parent this baby, if that makes sense,
sentences.zh: 我们有一会儿没回家，因为如果这么说能讲得通的话，我觉得我需要先学会怎么抚养这个宝宝，

sentences.en: whilst being worried he's going to die.
sentences.zh: 同时又很担心他会夭折。

sentences.en: Turns out he didn't have his surgery for eight weeks.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他的手术直到八周后才做。

sentences.en: And we obviously did go home a couple of days later.
sentences.zh: 我们显然在几天后还是回家了。

sentences.en: However, the day after that, a house extension started, which should have been done before he was born.
sentences.zh: 然而，就在那之后的第二天，房子开始扩建了，这本应该在他出生前就完成的。

sentences.en: Like our babies are not always born into ideal circumstances.
sentences.zh: 就像我们的孩子并不总是在理想的环境中出生一样。

sentences.en: And even though we might start with something that feels like cloud nine, things can change so quickly, can't they?
sentences.zh: 尽管我们的开始可能感觉像是置身云端，但事情变化得可以非常快，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they really can.
sentences.zh: 是的，真的会这样。

sentences.en: They really can.
sentences.zh: 真的会这样。

sentences.en: My eldest was born during COVID, during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我的大宝出生在新冠疫情期间，也就是大流行期间。

sentences.en: And that had an impact on so many babies and so many parent-infant relationships.
sentences.zh: 这对许多婴儿以及许多父母与婴儿的关系都产生了影响。

sentences.en: And we really can start from everything seeming like it's OK.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的生活确实可能从一切看起来都很好的状态开始。

sentences.en: We can start from a position of having a good enough child experience, a good enough experience of being parented ourselves,
sentences.zh: 我们可以从这样的起点开始：拥有还算不错的童年经历，拥有还算不错的被抚养经历，

sentences.en: a good enough birth experience, which unfortunately isn't that common.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个还算不错的生育体验，不幸的是，这并不那么常见。

sentences.en: You know, low levels, high levels of birth trauma are not uncommon.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，轻度或重度的生育创伤并不少见。

sentences.en: But we could have a good enough birthing experience, a supportive family around us.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以拥有一个还算不错的生产体验，周围有支持我们的家人。

sentences.en: But something can change, whether that's illness or something in your baby, whether that's a difficult pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 然而事情可能会改变，无论是疾病还是宝宝身上的某些状况，亦或是经历艰难的孕期。

sentences.en: I had two very difficult pregnancies and that was not my plan at all.
sentences.zh: 我有过两次非常艰难的孕期，这完全不在我的计划之内。

sentences.en: Well, I was definitely going to be the fit and healthy, still running, still working right up until the last moment.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我原本绝对要做那种健康健美、还能跑步、一直工作到最后一刻的人。

sentences.en: I'm absolutely fine.
sentences.zh: 我好得很。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: This pregnancy won't impact me at all sort of person.
sentences.zh: 这种怀孕对我一点影响也没有的那种人。

sentences.en: And that was not me at all.
sentences.zh: 而我完全不是那样。

sentences.en: I was incredibly poorly for both my pregnancies.
sentences.zh: 我的两次孕期都非常难受。

sentences.en: And I think probably because of the work that I do, I was able to separate out pregnancy and baby and still think positively about baby,
sentences.zh: 我想可能是因为我从事的工作，我能够把怀孕和宝宝分离开来，依然对宝宝保持积极的看法，

sentences.en: even though really disliking being pregnant.
sentences.zh: 尽管我其实非常讨厌怀孕。

sentences.en: But if I'd had less support, if I'd maybe not worked for the NHS and not been able to take off that time when I needed to,
sentences.zh: 但如果我的支持少一些，如果我可能不是为英国国民健康制度（NHS）工作、无法在需要时请假，

sentences.en: if the situations around me had been less supportive, it would have been really easy for me to really struggle with bonding with my babies in pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 如果我周围的环境没那么支持我，我在孕期要艰难地与宝宝建立亲子关系，就会是一件非常容易的事。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it really, this field, unfortunately, really can impact anyone.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这个领域，不幸的是，真的会影响到任何人。

sentences.en: Yes, there are things from our past that might make it more likely that we might struggle with bonding with our babies.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们过去的经历可能会让我们更有可能在与宝宝建立亲子关系时遇到困难。

sentences.en: So if we've had significant mental health problems in the past, if we've struggled with social support,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们过去经历过重大的心理健康问题，如果我们缺乏社会支持，

sentences.en: if we have unstable accommodation and all of those things that just make life in general quite challenging, those things can impact on parent-infant relationships.
sentences.zh: 如果我们居无定所有不稳定的住所，以及所有那些让日常生活变得颇具挑战的事情，这些都会对亲子关系产生影响。

sentences.en: But it can also feel like it comes a little bit out of the blue as well.
sentences.zh: 但有时这种感觉也可能有点像突如其来的一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So let's fast forward a little bit.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们快进一点。

sentences.en: Let's let's imagine that we've got we've got a child and their parent or parents in front of you in in clinic.
sentences.zh: 让我们想象一下，在诊所里，你面前坐着一个孩子以及他的父母或某一方父母。

sentences.en: What kind of options have we got available to us as treatment or intervention to help this unit to thrive?
sentences.zh: 作为治疗或干预手段，我们有哪些可用的选择来帮助这个家庭蓬勃发展？

sentences.en: So the field I work in, it's sometimes called infant mental health, sometimes called parent-infant relationship services, which is often kind of acronym to pairs.
sentences.zh: 我从事的领域，有时被称为婴儿心理健康，有时被称为亲子关系服务，通常缩写为PAIRS。

sentences.en: There are not enough of them.
sentences.zh: 这类服务数量还远远不够。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there's about 50 at time of recording.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在录制时大约有50个。

sentences.en: There's about 50 what we call fully established specialist parent-infant relationship services nationally.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，我们称之为全面建立的专业亲子关系服务的机构大约有50家。

sentences.en: A recent report said we needed 400 to cover every baby in the country.
sentences.zh: 最近的一份报告称，我们需要400家才能覆盖全国的每一个婴儿。

sentences.en: So, yeah, we have a long way of providing the service that lots of families need.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，要提供许多家庭所需要的服务，我们还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: But if a family is lucky enough to live in a serve in an area where there is an NHS or local authority service available,
sentences.zh: 但如果一个家庭足够幸运，居住在有NHS或地方当局服务覆盖的地区，

sentences.en: or they're in a position through private health care insurance or through their own means to kind of fund a an intervention,
sentences.zh: 或者他们能够通过私人医疗保险或自己的经济能力来资助一项干预措施，

sentences.en: there's a range of different options available.
sentences.zh: 那么有各种不同的选择可供他们使用。

sentences.en: So I often think about these in kind of three groups, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以我通常把这些大致归纳为三类。

sentences.en: We've got the families who might have maybe not been around babies much, feeling a bit lacking in confidence, feeling a bit like, who is this baby and how do I look after them?
sentences.zh: 我们有这样一些家庭，他们可能接触婴儿不多，缺乏自信，觉得有点像，这个婴儿是谁，我该怎么照顾他们？

sentences.en: And all of those kind of lacking in confidence things that a lot of new parents experience.
sentences.zh: 以及许多新手父母都会经历的种种缺乏自信的表现。

sentences.en: But maybe if that's paired with a little bit of anxiety or a little bit of low mood and it's really impacting on a parent,
sentences.zh: 但如果这伴随着一丝焦虑或轻度情绪低落，并且确实对父母造成了影响，

sentences.en: then we might do some kind of psychoeducation work about how babies develop, about baby brain development,
sentences.zh: 那么我们可能会开展一些心理教育工作，关于婴儿如何发育，关于婴儿大脑发育，

sentences.en: about the importance of responding to a baby, about how actually if you are responsive and attuned to your baby in the earliest of days and years,
sentences.zh: 关于回应婴儿的重要性，关于实际上如果你在最早的日子和最初的几年里对你的婴儿做出回应并保持同频，

sentences.en: tends to set them up for a slightly easier journey later in life.
sentences.zh: 往往会为他们以后的人生奠定一条稍微轻松一点的道路。

sentences.en: I often think about that, that actually if we if we are responsive and attuned to our babies for those first one thousand and one days,
sentences.zh: 我经常这样想，实际上如果我们在这最初的一千零一天里对我们的婴儿做出回应并保持同频，

sentences.en: clearly not always, there's always going to be variation, but you're likely to have that relationship with your baby.
sentences.zh: 当然并非总是如此，总会有所差异，但你很可能会与你的婴儿建立起那种关系。

sentences.en: That means that the toddler years, the teenage years, your adult years, you can maintain that relationship throughout.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在幼儿期、青少年期、成年期，你可以始终保持这种关系。

sentences.en: It's hard work at the beginning, but it tends to pay off.
sentences.zh: 开始时虽然辛苦，但通常会有所回报。

sentences.en: But if that's feeling challenging for a family, we might talk about kind of that importance of responding.
sentences.zh: 但如果一个家庭觉得这很有挑战性，我们可能会讨论回应的重要性。

sentences.en: That kind of work often happens as well.
sentences.zh: 这类工作也经常进行。

sentences.en: If, for example, I'm working with a younger family, a younger parents,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我正在协助一个年轻的家庭、年轻的父母，

sentences.en: and we all know that there is no time in our lives where random people want to give us advice better than when we've just had a baby.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，在我们的一生中，没有什么时间比刚生完孩子时更让素不相识的人想要给我们提建议了。

sentences.en: Like strangers, distant relatives, everybody wants to tell you something about how you should parent or how you shouldn't parent when you've just had a baby.
sentences.zh: 就像陌生人、远房亲戚，每个人都想在你刚生完孩子时对你应该怎么带娃或不应该怎么带娃指手画脚。

sentences.en: And so that psychoeducation type work often is really helpful for families,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种心理教育类型的工作对家庭通常真的很有帮助，

sentences.en: either they're getting a lot of those mixed messages or maybe they're younger and they're relying on TikTok and things like that,
sentences.zh: 要么是他们接收到了太多混杂的信息，要么是他们比较年轻，依赖TikTok之类的平台，

sentences.en: or their grandparents who maybe parenting has kind of changed over the last couple of generations.
sentences.zh: 或者他们的祖父母那辈的育儿方式在过去几代人中已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: So we might do some work to kind of help them build confidence in actually, you know what, responding to my baby really is the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会做一些工作来帮他们建立信心，其实，你知道吗，对我的宝宝做出回应确实是正确的做法。

sentences.en: I don't need to listen to the older generation who might say, ignore a baby's cries, don't pick them up when they cry, those kind of messaging.
sentences.zh: 我不需要听老一辈的话，他们可能会说，忽略宝宝的哭声，他们哭的时候不要抱他们，诸如此类的言论。

sentences.en: So that's one type of work that we might offer.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们可能会提供的其中一种工作。

sentences.en: It tends to be quite short term.
sentences.zh: 这往往是相当短期的。

sentences.en: We also offer a couple of interventions that are often used, and there are absolutely variations on these, but there's a couple of interventions.
sentences.zh: 我们还提供几种经常使用的干预措施，这些措施当然会有所变化，但有几种核心的干预方法。

sentences.en: One's called Circle of Security, and that's usually run in a group.
sentences.zh: 其中一种叫做“安全圈”（Circle of Security），通常是以小组形式进行的。

sentences.en: It's a very therapeutic group.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有治疗意义的小组。

sentences.en: It helps families to think about, or parents to think about their own early experiences and how they might be impacting on how they're parenting their children.
sentences.zh: 它帮助家庭或父母思考他们自己的早期经历，以及这些经历可能会如何影响他们抚养孩子的方式。

sentences.en: So really gentle, compassionate, warm groups.
sentences.zh: 所以这是非常温和、富有同情心且温暖的小组。

sentences.en: We also can do work called video interaction guidance.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以开展一项名为“视频互动指导”（video interaction guidance）的工作。

sentences.en: There's another model called VIP, which, yes, similar sort of work,
sentences.zh: 还有另一个名为VIP的模式，是的，工作性质类似，

sentences.en: but this is a really lovely intervention where we record parents and babies or parents and young children interacting.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种非常棒的干预措施，我们会记录父母与婴儿或父母与幼儿互动的过程。

sentences.en: And then we take it back and we do some editing of the video and we come back and we show parents essentially all the lovely moments of connection.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将其带回去对视频进行一些剪辑，再回来向父母展示那些美好的连接时刻。

sentences.en: And it's such a beautiful intervention because we can, I've seen so often a parent who has said, oh, my baby doesn't smile at me or my baby doesn't seem to want me.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常美丽的干预手段，因为我经常看到有父母说，哦，我的宝宝不对我笑，或者我的宝宝好像不需要我。

sentences.en: They just want somebody else or I don't know how to respond to my baby.
sentences.zh: 他们只想要别人，或者我不知道该怎么回应我的宝宝。

sentences.en: And then I'll just film for less than 10 minutes, usually about six to eight minutes we'll film.
sentences.zh: 然后我只需要拍摄不到10分钟，通常大约拍摄六到八分钟。

sentences.en: And we come back the week after and I can show them two, three, and often there's loads of clips that I could have picked, but I'll pick the kind of two,
sentences.zh: 我们在第二周回来，我可以给他们看两三个，而且通常有大量我可以挑选的片段，但我会挑选那种，

sentences.en: three really lovely moments where this parent absolutely does understand what their baby needs, is responding.
sentences.zh: 两三个真正美好的时刻：这位父母确实完全理解他们的宝宝需要什么，并且做出了回应。

sentences.en: The baby is looking to their parent and it's just such a beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 宝宝正看着他们的父母，这真的是一件太美妙的事情了。

sentences.en: And then we also work with families in my field where parents had a really challenging life, essentially.
sentences.zh: 在我的领域里，我们还与这样的家庭合作：父母的生平经历可以说是非常具有挑战性的。

sentences.en: They might have had experiences of neglect, abuse in their own early childhoods, that they are relating to other people and to now their baby in a way that is not helpful for them,
sentences.zh: 他们可能在自己的幼儿时期经历过忽视、虐待，以至于他们与他人交往以及现在与宝宝交往的方式对他们自己没有帮助，

sentences.en: not helpful for their baby.
sentences.zh: 对他们的宝宝也没有帮助。

sentences.en: So I use a model called Cognitive Analytic Therapy, CAT, so that's the model that I use to help families to think,
sentences.zh: 所以我使用一种叫做认知分析治疗（CAT）的模式，这是我用来帮助家庭思考的模式，

sentences.en: to help parents think about their relationship patterns in general and how those are applying to their baby.
sentences.zh: 帮助父母思考他们总体的关系模式，以及这些模式是如何应用到他们的宝宝身上的。

sentences.en: But there are lots of other models that sit at that kind of long-term therapeutic level that help either with parent and baby in the room or just with parent in the room to think through those relational patterns and start to think about changing them for baby's well-being.
sentences.zh: 但在那种长期治疗层面还有许多其他的模式，无论是父母和宝宝都在房间里，还是只有父母在房间里，来帮助梳理这些关系模式，并开始为宝宝的福祉做出改变。

sentences.en: Gosh, that sounds lovely.
sentences.zh: 天哪，听起来太美好了。

sentences.en: You might well have the best job in the world there, or one of them.
sentences.zh: 你很可能拥有世界上最好的工作，或者其中之一。

sentences.en: It sounds like you found a happy home.
sentences.zh: 听起来你找到了一个让你感到快乐的归宿。

sentences.en: And I know from just before we clicked record that you said that actually this was the result of a placement that you did.
sentences.zh: 而且从我们在点击录音之前的一番交谈中我知道，你提到其实这是你曾参与过的一次实习的结果。

sentences.en: I think it was your last placement on training that really ignited your passion for this area.
sentences.zh: 我想正是你在培训期间的最后一次实习，即最后一次长达九个月的实习，真正点燃了你对这个领域的激情。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So I actually started in forensic services.
sentences.zh: 其实我最初是在法医服务部门工作的。

sentences.en: So I did my undergraduate degree, my master's degree in forensic psychology, and then did my, I was a healthcare assistant, assistant psychologist, again, forensics.
sentences.zh: 我读了本科，获得了法医心理学硕士学位，然后担任医疗助理、助理心理学家，依然是在法医领域。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until I got onto clinical training and, yeah, did my final placement, a nine-month placement in a 0-5 NHS service.
sentences.zh: 直到我进入临床培训，并且，是的，完成了我的最后一次实习——在NHS的0-5岁服务部门进行为期九个月的实习。

sentences.en: And my intention of going to that service was still from a pursuing forensics perspective of I wanted to essentially see where some of the issues that we see in forensics,
sentences.zh: 我去那个部门的初衷，依然是从追求法医的角度出发，我想从根本上了解我们在法医领域看到的一些问题，

sentences.en: where they started.
sentences.zh: 它们究竟是从哪里开始的。

sentences.en: I knew that they started very early.
sentences.zh: 我知道它们开始得很早。

sentences.en: So that was my kind of intention of going into that service.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我进入那个部门的初衷。

sentences.en: But I loved it.
sentences.zh: 但我爱上了它。

sentences.en: And I loved the preventative element of it and how much change can happen for a family during those first few years of life,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它的预防性质，以及在一个家庭生命的最初几年里，能够为他们带来多大的改变，

sentences.en: because parents are often really motivated and really want best for their baby and therefore for themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为父母通常都非常有动力，非常渴望为他们的宝宝好，从而也为他们自己好。

sentences.en: And the baby is so amenable to change in terms of their brain development that it absolutely it's a it's a wonderful, wonderful period to work with.
sentences.zh: 而且婴儿的大脑发育对环境变化的适应能力极强，因此这绝对是一个非常、非常适合开展工作的时期。

sentences.en: And one of the sad things as well, which I wish we didn't have to talk about, but I talked with a lot of commissioners nationally, is that it's cheaper as well.
sentences.zh: 令人遗憾的是，而且这也是我希望不必谈论的话题——但我跟全国许多地方专员交流过——那就是这更省钱。

sentences.en: It's a lot cheaper for society if we work with families at this pre-problem, pre-diagnosis, early intervention stage.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能在这种问题出现前、确诊前以及早期干预阶段介入并与家庭合作，这对社会来说要省钱得多。

sentences.en: If we can help a family, a parent to parent in a way that they want to parent in a more sensitive and attuned way,
sentences.zh: 如果我们能以一种家长所期望的、更敏感且更能共情的方式来协助他们，支持家长做好父母，

sentences.en: and that baby receives that sensitive and attuned parenting and goes on to achieve all of the wonderful things that humans were able to achieve,
sentences.zh: 并且让那个婴儿获得这种敏感且共情的养育，进而实现人类所能达到的所有美好成就，

sentences.en: then that family costs the system less.
sentences.zh: 那么这个家庭对系统造成的成本就会降低。

sentences.en: And I hate that we have to talk about it because it should absolutely be just about the human impact.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌我们必须谈论这个，因为这本来应该完全只关乎对人类的影响。

sentences.en: So this is very much just an added bonus as opposed to the reason why we do this work.
sentences.zh: 所以这更多只是一个额外的附带好处，而不是我们开展这项工作的初衷。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think it's taken me back to when I worked in forensic youth services and it wasn't uncommon to to read the background case stories of the young people in our care
sentences.zh: 而且我想这让我回想起以前在法医青少年服务机构工作的时候，阅读我们照顾的年轻人的背景案例故事并不少见，

sentences.en: who might have been a few hours old in their baby carrier left on the steps of the police station or the fire station whilst mum or dad went on to do a drugs run and then come back and get them later.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在几个小时大时就被放在婴儿提篮里，遗弃在警察局或消防局的台阶上，而妈妈或爸爸则去贩毒，然后再回来接他们。

sentences.en: And actually, that child was always going to have a very tough experience of life.
sentences.zh: 说实话，那个孩子注定要经历非常艰难的人生。

sentences.en: And it's whether if we can get services like yours and like the other 49 around the country and hopefully the other 350 coming soon to really think about holistically supporting that family
sentences.zh: 如果我们能让像你这样的服务机构，以及全国其他49家、还有希望很快增加的350家机构，真正去思考如何全方位地支持这个家庭，

sentences.en: or giving them viable options for for helping support them, you know, in the care system to help that child and the adults to thrive
sentences.zh: 或者为他们提供切实可行的选择来帮助支持他们，你知道的，在照料体系中帮助那个孩子和成年人茁壮成长，

sentences.en: so that everybody can have a better, less distressing experience of life.
sentences.zh: 从而让每个人都能拥有更好、痛苦更少的人生体验，那会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And that that's my dream.
sentences.zh: 而那正是我的梦想。

sentences.en: That's that's what I always hope to create.
sentences.zh: 那正是我一直希望能创造的。

sentences.en: And our work, working in psychology, working in mental health, working with people who've experienced distress in general, it it's hard.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的工作，从事心理学工作，从事心理健康工作，与经历过痛苦的人们一起工作，总的来说，这很不容易。

sentences.en: It's hard work at times.
sentences.zh: 有时候这真的是一项艰巨的工作。

sentences.en: And we but I always hold on to that.
sentences.zh: 但我们——我总是坚持这一点。

sentences.en: And when I deliver training to different professionals and we talk about how difficult our our work is, how difficult it is to for families to change,
sentences.zh: 当我向不同的专业人员进行培训，我们谈论我们的工作有多么困难，家庭要改变有多么困难，

sentences.en: to change patterns that have been ingrained throughout the generations, whether it's those families that are doing those drug steals or involved in criminal kind of history,
sentences.zh: 要改变世世代代根深蒂固的模式有多么困难，无论是那些去偷毒品的家庭，还是涉及某种犯罪历史的家庭，

sentences.en: those things passed down through the generations.
sentences.zh: 这些东西代代相传。

sentences.en: That's not one person deciding to go out and do that.
sentences.zh: 那可不是某一个人决定出门去做那种事。

sentences.en: That's a culture.
sentences.zh: 那是一种文化。

sentences.en: And breaking that cycle, changing that way of being, that way of existing as a person, as a family.
sentences.zh: 而打破这种循环，改变那种生存方式、作为一个人或一个家庭的存在方式，

sentences.en: It's really, really hard work.
sentences.zh: 真的是非常、非常艰难的工作。

sentences.en: So the people that I work with, you know, we talk on training and supervision.
sentences.zh: 所以与我共事的人，你知道的，我们在培训和督导中会讨论到。

sentences.en: We talk about how challenging it is to break those cycles.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论打破这些循环有多么具有挑战性。

sentences.en: But it's amazing when it happens.
sentences.zh: 但当它发生时，真的很神奇。

sentences.en: It's so wonderful when it happens.
sentences.zh: 当它发生时，是如此美好。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think some of that self-esteem work, isn't it, is that the people around us, we might well take their opinion as something quite important and powerful.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想其中一些关于自尊的工作，对吧，就是我们身边的人，我们很可能会把他们的意见看得相当重要和有分量。

sentences.en: But it's almost understanding that sometimes the advice we're given might serve the other person more than it genuinely serves our own intereSt.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于去理解，有时我们得到的建议可能更多地是为了满足对方的利益，而不是真正符合我们自身的利益。

sentences.en: And just being able to be curious or notice that can be life changing.
sentences.zh: 只要能够保持好奇心或注意到这一点，就能改变一生。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And I think parenting is maybe it's just because it's my field, but parenting seems to be the time when that happens most that actually everybody has got an opinion.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为育儿——也许这只是因为这是我的专业领域——但育儿似乎是这种情况发生得最多的时期，每个人实际上都有自己的看法。

sentences.en: Baby sleep.
sentences.zh: 婴儿睡眠。

sentences.en: I do a lot of work on on baby sleep, supporting families with sleep.
sentences.zh: 我做了很多关于婴儿睡眠的工作，在睡眠方面支持家庭。

sentences.en: And that is a really challenging field to be in.
sentences.zh: 而那确实是一个极具挑战性的领域。

sentences.en: I'm sure people listening to this will have seen the kind of BBC News articles and investigations over the last year about about how unregulated and unmonitored it is to work with with families around sleep.
sentences.zh: 我敢听这个节目的人在过去一年里都看到过BBC新闻关于围绕睡眠与家庭合作是多么不受监管和缺乏监督的各种报道和调查。

sentences.en: And there is some, quite frankly, very dodgy and scary advice out there around how how to get your baby to sleep and how to respond to your baby or not while they're sleeping.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，外面流传着一些非常不靠谱且吓人的建议，关于如何让你的婴儿入睡，以及在他们睡觉时如何回应婴儿（或者不回应）。

sentences.en: And so, yes, that can be one area in particular where parents confidence can be really undermined because their family might be saying one thing,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这可能是一个特别的领域，父母的自信心很容易受到打击，因为他们的家人可能会说一种意见，

sentences.en: their friends who've just had a baby might be doing it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 他们刚生完孩子的朋辈可能会用另一种方式去做，

sentences.en: Their instincts say that actually this baby needs me.
sentences.zh: 而他们的直觉却在说，实际上这个婴儿需要我。

sentences.en: I want to pick up my baby.
sentences.zh: 我想抱起我的婴儿。

sentences.en: I want to hold my baby.
sentences.zh: 我想抱着我的婴儿。

sentences.en: But the messages from from social media, from family, from friends can be quite different and quite anxiety provoking to think, you know,
sentences.zh: 但来自社交媒体、家人、朋友的信息却可能大相径庭，并且相当容易引发焦虑，让你觉得，你知道的，

sentences.en: this little baby needs me so much and I want the absolute best for them.
sentences.zh: 这个小婴儿太需要我了，我想要给他/她绝对最好的东西。

sentences.en: And I don't know what's beSt. But we are.
sentences.zh: 而我不知道什么才是最好的。但我们正在努力。

sentences.en: There is no manual.
sentences.zh: 根本没有什么育儿手册。

sentences.en: There's no manual for parenting.
sentences.zh: 育儿是没有手册的。

sentences.en: And I think any there's been so many books published and research around babies and parenthood.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于婴儿和为人父母，已经出版了如此之多的书籍，也做过无数的研究。

sentences.en: And it can be really tempting for people to keep writing and people in general public to keep reading about what how should I raise my baby?
sentences.zh: 对于人们来说，特别是大众，不断去写、去读关于“我该如何抚养我的婴儿”、“什么对这最好”的内容，确实是非常具有诱惑力的。

sentences.en: What's the best thing for this?
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这其实取决于：

sentences.en: But it essentially comes down to.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻你的婴儿在表达他们需要什么，而你是否能在大部分时间里对这种需求做出回应？

sentences.en: What is your baby in this moment saying they need and can you respond to that need enough of the time?
sentences.zh: 如果你能做到这一点，那么这就是适合你和你的家庭的方法。

sentences.en: And if you're able to do that, then that's what works for you and your family.
sentences.zh: 有那么多的书试图对此进行拓展，并试图找出完美的公式，来精确规定我们应该做什么、我们应该如何回应婴儿以及我们应该如何抚养婴儿。

sentences.en: And there's so many books that will try and expand on that and get the perfect formula for exactly what we should do and how we should respond to our babies and how we should raise our babies.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上更多关乎你们两人此时此刻之间正在发生的事情。

sentences.zh: 对于专业人士，我想说的是，如果你是一位与父母和婴儿打交道的专业人士，

sentences.en: and it might not be your entire focus, you know, you might not be a health visitor who's bread and butter this is.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是你的全部工作重点，你知道的，你可能不是那种以此为生的健康访视员。

sentences.en: You might be somebody who works in drug and alcohol services or homelessness services, but you're working with parents who have young children.
sentences.zh: 你可能是从事毒品和酒精服务或无家可归者服务的人，但你在接触有幼儿的父母。

sentences.en: I think one of the biggest things we can do is to recognise the impact of having a baby, and that is with that family, but also on a more global level.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们能做的最重要的事情之一，就是认识到拥有一个宝宝所带来的影响，不仅是对这个家庭，而且是在更广泛的层面上。

sentences.en: So we call it the baby blind spot.
sentences.zh: 所以我们称之为“婴儿盲区”。

sentences.en: When we write policies from the government, when we create services, we usually don't take into account the needs of babies.
sentences.zh: 当政府制定政策、当我们创建服务时，通常都没有把婴儿的需求考虑在内。

sentences.en: So if you are working with parents and they have a really young baby, you know, think with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在接触父母，而他们有一个非常小的宝宝，你知道的，要为他们着想。

sentences.en: Really simple stuff like a 9am appointment might not be the best time.
sentences.zh: 非常简单的事情，比如上午9点的预约可能不是最佳时间。

sentences.en: They might need a little bit longer to get there in the morning.
sentences.zh: 他们早上可能需要多花一点时间才能赶到。

sentences.en: But if they're running late and they've brought their baby with them,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们迟到了，而且把宝宝也带来了，

sentences.en: and, you know, it might not be ideal if you're offering whatever service you're offering, drugs and alcohol therapy service, but can you work with that?
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，如果你提供的服务（比如毒品和酒精治疗服务）可能不太适合带孩子，但你能配合一下吗？

sentences.en: Can you do something to accommodate the fact that this parent is going through a change in their lives and has that baby with them?
sentences.zh: 你能做点什么来关照这样一个事实：这位父母的人生正在经历转变，而且身边带着宝宝？

sentences.en: In terms of for parents, it really is about staying, I was going to say confident.
sentences.zh: 至于父母方面，真的就是要保持——我本来想说保持自信。

sentences.en: It's hard to remain confident, but holding on to what kind of parent do I want to be?
sentences.zh: 要保持自信很难，但要坚持住：我想成为什么样的父母？

sentences.en: What kind of parent do I want my children in the future to look back on and think that's the kind of parent that you were?
sentences.zh: 在未来，我希望我的孩子回想起我时，觉得我是一个什么样的父母？

sentences.en: And as much as is possible, definitely not all of the time, but as much as is possible, being that parent and kind of being that parent
sentences.zh: 并且在尽可能的情况下（当然绝不是每时每刻都能做到），但尽可能地去做那样的父母，

sentences.en: and responding to what your baby needs in the moment.
sentences.zh: 及时回应你宝宝此刻的需求。

sentences.en: That's what a baby needs.
sentences.zh: 这就是宝宝所需要的。

sentences.en: They just need us to be there to respond to nurture and trying as a parent not to get too worried about perfection
sentences.zh: 他们只需要我们在那里给予回应、悉心呵护，作为父母，尽量不要过分担心完美主义，

sentences.en: or how it should be done or how somebody else might be doing it, for example.
sentences.zh: 或者事情该怎么做，或者别人是怎么做的，等等。

sentences.en: Really nice.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Where can our audience learn more about you and your work, Charlotte?
sentences.zh: 我们的观众在哪里可以更多地了解你和你的工作，夏洛特？

sentences.en: So I run a non-profit organisation.
sentences.zh: 我经营着一家非营利组织。

sentences.en: I'm based up in Scarborough, North Yorkshire.
sentences.zh: 我的基地在北约克郡的斯卡伯勒。

sentences.en: So in terms of working therapeutic with families, I absolutely do do that nationally.
sentences.zh: 所以就为家庭提供治疗服务而言，我确实在全国范围内开展工作。

sentences.en: It would be via video link if they're not local to me.
sentences.zh: 如果他们离我这里不远，可以通过视频连线进行。

sentences.en: So if there is families watching that are worried about their parent-infant relationship, their bond with baby, their baby's sleep, etc., you're very welcome to get in touch.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有观看节目的家庭担心他们与婴儿的关系、与宝宝的纽带、宝宝的睡眠等问题，非常欢迎随时联系我。

sentences.en: I also have a few resources on my website as well.
sentences.zh: 我的网站上也提供了一些资源。

sentences.en: So there's a blog if people are interested in hearing more.
sentences.zh: 如果大家有兴趣了解更多，上面有一个博客。

sentences.en: We put a lot of stuff on social media, from brain development, bonding and attachment, sleep, all of that stuff is up on my social media accounts.
sentences.zh: 我们在社交媒体上发布了大量内容，从大脑发育、亲子依恋到睡眠，所有这些都可以在我的社交媒体账号上找到。

sentences.en: And then I have a webinar for professionals.
sentences.zh: 然后我还有一个针对专业人士的网络研讨会。

sentences.en: So if you're a professional, a health visitor, a midwife, an aspiring psychologist, a mental health practitioner, whoever you might be that works with parents and babies,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一位专业人士，比如健康访视员、助产士、有志成为心理学家的人、心理健康从业者，无论你是谁，只要你与父母和婴儿打交道，

sentences.en: there's a one-hour introduction to infant mental health on my website.
sentences.zh: 我的网站上有一个关于婴儿心理健康的为期一小时的入门课程。

sentences.en: And then there's also a sleep workshop for families.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个针对家庭的睡眠工作坊。

sentences.en: So if you are about to have a baby or you've just had a baby and you're wondering how this sleep thing works for babies,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你即将迎来一个宝宝，或者刚刚有了宝宝，想知道宝宝的睡眠是怎么一回事，

sentences.en: then yeah, it takes two hours-ish to kind of work through pre-recorded.
sentences.zh: 那么，是的，大约花两个小时左右就能看完全部的预录内容。

sentences.en: So if you're wanting a kind of more personalised consultation, you're very welcome to contact me.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要更个性化的咨询，非常欢迎联系我。

sentences.en: But if you want in just a general overview of how babies sleep, then that resource is there as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是想对宝宝如何睡觉有一个大致的了解，那个资源也在那里。

sentences.en: So the website's borntobond.co.uk and emailing me and all the social media and the blogs and everything kind of would link back from that webpage.
sentences.zh: 网址是 borntobond.co.uk，发邮件给我以及所有的社交媒体、博客和一切内容都可以从这个网页链接过去。

sentences.en: So that's the best place to go.
sentences.zh: 所以那是最好的去处。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Charlotte.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，夏洛特。

sentences.en: And thank you for your time talking about this really, really important area.
sentences.zh: 也感谢你抽出时间来谈论这个非常非常重要的领域。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for watching.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的观看。

sentences.en: And thank you again to my guest for today, Dr. Charlotte Dunster-Page.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢我今天的嘉宾，夏洛特·邓斯特-佩奇博士。

sentences.en: I have been blown away by this episode.
sentences.zh: 这一集让我大开眼界、深受震撼。

sentences.en: I would love to know what you think.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你的想法。

sentences.en: Please do drop a comment either on YouTube or on Spotify for this episode.
sentences.zh: 请务必在 YouTube 或 Spotify 上给这一集留言。

sentences.en: Let us know what you think.
sentences.zh: 让我们知道你的想法。

sentences.en: And you can come and follow me on social media and let me know there too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在社交媒体上关注我，并在那里告诉我。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent everywhere on socials.
sentences.zh: 我在所有社交平台上都是“玛丽安·特伦特博士”（Dr. Marianne Trent）。

sentences.en: If you found this episode helpful, I think you'll really enjoy the one I did with Dr. Jade Redfern about calm parenting and endeavouring to shout less, be less shouty parent.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这一集对你有帮助，我想你会非常喜欢我和杰德·雷德芬博士（Dr. Jade Redfern）录制的关于平静育儿、努力少吼叫、做一个少吼叫的父母的那一集。

sentences.en: I adore Jade's work and I hope you will too.
sentences.zh: 我非常欣赏杰德的工作，希望你也会喜欢。

sentences.en: If you are working in psychology and mental health, please do consider whether the aspiring psychologist membership might be helpful to you,
sentences.zh: 如果你从事心理学和心理健康工作，请考虑一下有志心理学家会员资格是否对你有所帮助，

sentences.en: which you can join from just £30 a month with no minimum term.
sentences.zh: 你只需每月30英镑即可加入，且无最低期限要求。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出售时间以外的方式赚钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名临床心理学家，我自2019年以来一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的一对多项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022, and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我在2022年亲自完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两批心理学家走过他们的成长之旅。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses, plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利，以及我独家的全套支持，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四场小组智囊会、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南-梅森（Fortnum and Mason）礼品，以及限时一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。
